title: The 1988/1989 Excavation at Giza
venue: Journal of the American Research Center in Egypt, 38
authorBackground: Egyptologist; affiliated with the Giza Plateau Mapping Project
summary: Reports excavations at Giza that investigated settlement and work areas associated with pyramid construction. The public-facing app should use this as archaeological context, not as support for unsourced estimates of workforce size or legal status.

title: Great Zimbabwe National Monument
summary: The site record describes Great Zimbabwe and summarizes archaeological finds including imported glass beads and porcelain and gold and coins associated with Indian Ocean trade.

title: Term history: Khoisan / Khoesan
summary: The article discusses naming choices in the study of 19th-century |xam narratives and notes historical uses of the collective label. It is a critical commentary, not a source for describing every community’s identity.

title: Reconstructing the Historical Structure of the Bantu Language Family: Old Challenges, New Insights
authorBackground: Department of English and American Studies, University of Vienna
summary: A review of linguistic, archaeological, and genetic research that cautions against treating current narratives of Bantu history as settled.

title: Early evidence of San material culture represented by organic artifacts from Border Cave, South Africa
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 109(33), 13214–13219
summary: The study re-examines organic artefacts from Border Cave, including notched bones, and interprets some as evidence of notational use. Its interpretation should not be inflated into a claim that the object proves a formal number system.

title: Archaeological science, globalisation, and local agency: gold in Great Zimbabwe
authorBackground: Archaeological research by scholars affiliated with the Universities of Cambridge, Oxford, and Cape Town
summary: Peer-reviewed research on gold processing and Great Zimbabwe’s participation in regional and Indian Ocean exchange, emphasizing local production and agency.
